data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy governing the oversight and management of the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291.
cross_references: Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291
policy_statements.target: United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy

policy_statements.source_text: FITARA requires that the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) coordinate FITARA-related activities with other senior Department officials including the following:
Chief Financial Officer (CFO),
Chief Acquisition Officer (CAO),
Chief Operating Officer (COO) (represented by the USDA Deputy Secretary),
Senior Procurement Executive (SPE),
Chief Human Capital Officer (CHCO), and
the Director, Office of Budget and Program Analysis (OBPA).
The USDA CIO, CFO, COO, CAO, SPE, CHCO, and OBPA, as a group, will be identified in this DR as the Chief Executive Officers (CXO).
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA CIO, CFO, COO, CAO, SPE, CHCO, and OBPA

policy_statements.source_text: The CXOs are tasked with fully defining and understanding the costs of the Department’s information technology (IT) investments, products, and services to be included and incorporated into the USDA budget formulation, budget execution, acquisition, governance, program management, information security, cybersecurity, and IT workforce planning processes.
policy_statements.target: costs of the Department’s information technology (IT) investments, products, and services

policy_statements.source_text: This DR supersedes DR 3145-001, Oversight and Management of the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), dated September 13, 2016.
cross_references: DR 3145-001, Oversight and Management of the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA)

policy_statements.source_text: This DR is effective immediately upon publication and remains in effect until it is superseded or expires.
All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their policies and procedures, as appropriate, with this DR within 6 months of the published date.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: as appropriate
within 6 months of the published date

policy_statements.source_text: Nothing in this DR is intended to supplant the delegation of authorities and responsibilities of the USDA CIO under 7 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) § 2.32, Chief Information Officer, or any other authorities otherwise provided by law, Federal regulation, or USDA Departmental directives.
cross_references: 7 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) § 2.32, Chief Information Officer

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and are tasked with the accomplishment and implementation of the requirements identified in FITARA, OMB, and USDA guidance.
policy_statements.target: all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others
conditions: who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and are tasked with the accomplishment and implementation of the requirements identified in FITARA, OMB, and USDA guidance

policy_statements.source_text: FITARA was enacted on December 19, 2014, and outlines specific requirements related to Federal CIO authority enhancements; enhanced transparency and improved risk management in IT investments; portfolio reviews; the Federal Data Center Consolidation Initiative (DCOI); expansion of training and use of IT cadres; maximizing the benefit of the Federal strategic sourcing initiative (SSI); Category Management and the Governmentwide software purchasing program.

In order to provide more specific guidance for the implementation of FITARA, Office of Management and Budget (OMB) issued Memorandum M-15-14, Management and Oversight of Federal Information Technology.
cross_references: Memorandum M-15-14, Management and Oversight of Federal Information Technology

policy_statements.source_text: M-15-14 states that each covered Agency will:
Conduct a self-assessment to identify current conformity and compliance;

Develop an Agency Common Baseline implementation plan describing the changes to be made to ensure that all OMB Common Baseline for IT Management and CIO Assignment Plan (OMB Common Baseline) requirements would be implemented by December 31, 2015; and
cross_references: OMB Common Baseline for IT Management and CIO Assignment Plan (OMB Common Baseline)

policy_statements.source_text: Update the implementation progress in the Actions and Milestones Table document.
OMB also established an Actions and Milestones Table to track and identify the progression of tasks related to the success of the common baseline implementation.

On May 15, 2018, Executive Order (E.O.) 13833, Enhancing the Effectiveness of Agency Chief Information Officers, was signed by the President to implement successful IT management practices from the private sector, enabling Agencies to reduce costs, better protect sensitive data, and improve services offered to the public.
cross_references: Executive Order (E.O.) 13833, Enhancing the Effectiveness of Agency Chief Information Officers

policy_statements.source_text: The E.O. provides covered Agency CIOs, as described in the Chief Financial Officers (CFO) Act of 1990, P.L. 101-576, greater visibility into and control over their Agency’s IT resources, enhancing their effectiveness and better positioning them to modernize their IT systems, execute IT programs more efficiently, reduce cybersecurity risks, and serve the American people well.
cross_references: Chief Financial Officers (CFO) Act of 1990, P.L. 101-576

policy_statements.source_text: In response to FITARA and objectives further delineated in M-15-14, USDA developed the United States Department of Agriculture Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act Common Baseline and Implementation Plan (USDA Common Baseline Plan), dated November 14, 2015, which further delineates the role of the USDA CIO in establishing an inclusive, integrated governance process that manages IT as a strategic resource.
cross_references: United States Department of Agriculture Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act Common Baseline and Implementation Plan (USDA Common Baseline Plan), dated November 14, 2015

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Common Baseline Plan establishes a framework for USDA to implement the specific authorities that FITARA gives to the USDA CIO under the CFO Act of 1990 and builds upon the responsibilities outlined in the Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.
cross_references: Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.

policy_statements.source_text: The OMB Common Baseline and USDA Common Baseline Plan speak to the roles and responsibilities of the CXOs, which includes the USDA CIO.

In conjunction with the activities listed above, the USDA CIO, or designee, will engage at the Departmental level and throughout all Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices using IT governance bodies and decision-making processes in the key areas of finance, budget, acquisition, and human resources.
The USDA CIO will engage directly with these stakeholders, ensuring active involvement in policy decisions that are related to IT.

The USDA Deputy Secretary will ensure engagement at the Department level and within the Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to consistently align USDA’s budget, finance, acquisitions, governance, program management, human resources, information security, cybersecurity, and IT communities to FITARA.

The USDA CIO will use the enhanced authority provided under FITARA to ensure greater transparency and risk management of IT investments; review of Mission Area, agency, and staff office IT portfolios; consolidation of data centers; expansion of IT-related training (e.g., acquisition, program management, networks, systems, contracting) and use of IT cadres; maximizing the benefit of the Federal SSIs; Category Management; and Federal software purchasing programs.
The USDA Deputy Secretary will ensure all applicable policies, procedures, and governance structures are consistent with FITARA’s requirements.
policy_statements.target: all applicable policies, procedures, and governance structures

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CIO may, where authorized by FITARA, delegate authority for fulfilling FITARA requirements.
conditions: where authorized by FITARA

policy_statements.source_text: All roles and responsibilities identified in FITARA, and further delineated in M-15-14, are in effect.
The USDA SPE may fulfill the CAO requirements identified in M-15-14, and the USDA OBPA Director may fulfill the budget formulation requirements normally performed by the CFO.
The USDA Deputy Secretary, serving as the USDA COO, will:
Serve as the Chair of the Executive Information Technology Investment Review Board (E-Board);
policy_statements.target: Executive Information Technology Investment Review Board (E-Board)

policy_statements.source_text: Finalize recommendations to the Secretary concerning major IT investments proceeding through the USDA IT governance process;
Review and prioritize the USDA major IT investments portfolio consulting with USDA Under Secretaries and the USDA CIO, as necessary.
Approve self-assessment and plan documents; and
Oversee progress towards implementing FITARA actions within the USDA Common Baseline Plan and the Actions and Milestones Table.
The Assistant Secretary for Administration (ASA), serving as the CAO, will:
Manage the overall IT acquisition strategy and IT contract portfolio for the Department;
Review the IT acquisition process in coordination with the USDA CIO, SPE, and CFO to ensure FITARA requirements are met;
Delegate policy and oversight aspects of IT acquisitions to the USDA SPE, as appropriate; and
Address other CAO responsibilities as outlined and updated in the USDA Common Baseline Plan and the Actions and Milestones Table.
The USDA CIO will:
Leadership and Accountability
Report directly to the Secretary and or Deputy Secretary of Agriculture regarding IT matters and receive management guidance from the Deputy Secretary, serving as the Department’s COO;
Designate a USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO);
Develop a USDA assignment plan to delegate aspects of the USDA Common Baseline Plan to other CXOs;

Provide a delegation of authority memorandum to the Mission Area Assistant CIOs, in a rules-based manner, if a Mission Area, agency, or staff office assumes responsibility for a USDA Common Baseline Plan activity;
conditions: if a Mission Area, agency, or staff office assumes responsibility for a USDA Common Baseline Plan activity

policy_statements.source_text: Use PortfolioStat to improve the management of the USDA IT portfolio;
Use TechStat sessions to review high-risk IT investments to recommend termination or corrective actions; and
Address other USDA CIO and OCIO responsibilities as outlined and updated in the USDA Common Baseline Plan and the Actions and Milestones Table.
IT Strategic Planning
Establish goals for improving USDA operations through IT;
Measure performance of how well IT supports USDA programs;
Prepare an annual report on the progress of achieving the USDA IT strategic planning goals;
Benchmark USDA IT processes against the private and public sector; and
Ensure that USDA IT processes are analyzed and revised as appropriate before making significant IT investments.
conditions: as appropriate
before making significant IT investments

policy_statements.source_text: IT Budget
Fully participate in IT planning, programming, and budgeting decisions;
Participate in the planning, programming, and budgeting stages for programs that include IT resources;
conditions: for programs that include IT resources

policy_statements.source_text: Designate a representative for participating in Mission Area, agency, and staff office investment review boards that include IT resources;
conditions: that include IT resources

policy_statements.source_text: Review and approve funding for IT reprogramming requests (i.e., changes in funding levels for IT resources that require Congressional notification);

Define, in consultation with the CFO and OBPA Director, the level of detail with which IT resource levels are described distinctly from other resources throughout the planning, programming, and budgeting stages;
Evaluate whether to continue, modify, or terminate any acquisition, investment, or activity that includes a significant IT component and advise the Secretary;
conditions: that includes a significant IT component

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with the Secretary and the USDA CFO to ensure that financial systems are approved and effectively implemented;
Manage IT investments and advise and assist the USDA Secretary, Deputy Secretary, Under Secretaries, Mission Area Assistant CIOs, and executive governance boards, in the following:
Executing IT investments;
IT governance oversight; and
Improving IT personnel capabilities;
Define Departmentwide policy for the level of detail of planned IT expenditure reporting for all transactions that include IT resources;
conditions: for all transactions that include IT resources

policy_statements.source_text: Review and approve the IT budget requests in collaboration with the Director, OBPA and other appropriate CXO as it relates to their scope of responsibility (e.g., financial, acquisition, human resources, property); and
Establish and maintain a process to regularly engage with program managers to evaluate IT resources supporting each Mission Area, agency, and staff office strategic objective.
Acquisition
Maintain an inventory of data centers and a strategy to consolidate and optimize them;
Manage the IT execution decision and the governance and oversight processes related to IT;
Define overall policies for capital planning, enterprise architecture, project management, and reporting for IT resources;
Participate, or designate a representative, on executive level governance boards that include IT resources, including Mission Area, agency, and staff office investment review boards;
Certify that IT investments are adequately implementing incremental development, as defined in capital planning guidance issued by OMB; and
Review and approve IT contracts, acquisition plans, and acquisition strategies.
IT Organization and Workforce
Annually assess the requirements established for Mission Area personnel regarding IT management knowledge and skills;
Annually assess the extent to which USDA personnel meet IT management and information security knowledge and skill requirements;
Annually report to the Secretary of Agriculture on progress made in improving IT personnel capabilities;
Annually develop strategies for hiring and training to rectify any knowledge and skill deficiencies;
Collaborate with the Office of Human Resources Management (OHRM) in establishing a documented process for:
Review and concurrence of performance assessments for Mission Area Assistant CIO positions at the Senior Executive Service (SES), Senior Level (SL), and General Schedule (GS)-15 level; and
USDA CIO involvement in the recruitment and selection of SES, SL, and GS-15 Mission Area Assistant CIO positions;
Provide guidance to Mission Areas on recruitment and selection activities for Mission Area Assistant CIO positions in collaboration with OHRM.
“Mission Area Assistant CIO” is defined as SES, SL, or GS-15 positions classified as having a key IT role for a component organization;

Provide guidance to Mission Areas in establishing and implementing a formal documented process for the USDA CIO’s involvement in the performance evaluation of Mission Area Assistant CIOs in collaboration with the OHRM;
Recommend approval or disapproval of a proposed Mission Area Assistant CIO recruitment or reassignment action based on the needs of the Department before any staffing activities begin;
policy_statements.target: proposed Mission Area Assistant CIO recruitment or reassignment action
conditions: based on the needs of the Department
before any staffing activities begin

policy_statements.source_text: Review and approve the hiring manager’s tentative executive and non-executive Mission Area Assistant CIO selection;
Develop proposed mandatory language for the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) performance goals annually; no later than 30 days before the beginning of the new performance year;
conditions: annually
no later than 30 days before the beginning of the new performance year

policy_statements.source_text: Provide ongoing feedback, with documentation, to Mission Area Assistant CIOs throughout the performance year;
Provide input into the Mission Area Assistant CIO performance evaluations;
Ensure the USDA IT Leadership Directory as identified in the OMB Common Baseline is populated, kept up-to-date, and posted in concert with the CHCO; and
Establish a set of technical, and as applicable, leadership, competency requirements for all IT staff to ensure that USDA can:
Anticipate and respond to changing mission requirements;
Maintain workforce skills in a rapidly developing IT environment; and
Recruit and retain the IT talent needed to accomplish the mission.
Information Security
Ensure that senior USDA officials, including the Mission Area Assistant CIOs, carry out their information security responsibilities, through delegation of authority to the USDA CISO; and
Ensure that USDA personnel are held accountable for complying with the Departmentwide information security program, through delegation of authority to the USDA CISO.
The USDA CFO will:
Collaborate with the USDA CIO and his or her staff in overall portfolio planning of IT investments;
Provide guidance and advice for capturing spending data that will be electronically accessible by the USDA CIO to assist in evaluating the compliance of investments; and
Address other CFO and Office of the Chief Financial Officer (OCFO) responsibilities as outlined and updated in the USDA Common Baseline Plan and the Actions and Milestones Table.
The Director, OBPA will:

Coordinate with the USDA CIO in the development of guidance for Mission Area, agency, and staff office submissions of IT-related budget materials throughout all stages of the budget formulation process;
Collaborate with the USDA CIO in the review and analysis of budget and other funding proposals with IT impacts;
Collaborate with the USDA CIO on the annual development and signature of a joint certification letter;
Collaborate with the USDA CIO for the Department’s Strategic Planning and Performance Management activities;
Meet with the USDA CIO before the start of the annual budget formulation process to develop joint guidance and agree to a calendar of deliverables and data requests for USDA;
Coordinate with the USDA CIO in the development of guidance on budgetary reprogramming activities and associated Congressional notification requirements where there is an impact on IT; and
Address other OBPA responsibilities as outlined and updated in the USDA Common Baseline Plan and the Actions and Milestones Table.
The Director, Office of Contracting and Procurement (OCP), serving as the SPE, will:
Establish policy regarding the acquisition of IT products and services and ensuring that IT procurements comply with all applicable laws, regulations, guidance, and procedures;
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, Office of Contracting and Procurement (OCP)

policy_statements.source_text: Collaborate with the USDA CIO to issue IT policy related to the acquisition of IT products and services, including policy to ensure IT acquisitions are approved by the USDA CIO prior to obligating funds;
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, Office of Contracting and Procurement (OCP)

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure contract actions that contain IT are consistent with CIO approved acquisition strategies and plans; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, Office of Contracting and Procurement (OCP)

policy_statements.source_text: Address other USDA SPE and OCP responsibilities as outlined and updated in the USDA Common Baseline Plan and the Actions and Milestones Table.
policy_statements.actor_name: Director, Office of Contracting and Procurement (OCP)

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Director, OHRM, serving as the CHCO, will:
Administer USDA human resources and human capital policies for all IT positions;
Provide technical guidance and direction for IT-related human resources functions to ensure compliance with Federal regulations and USDA policies;

Notify the USDA CIO of any proposed SES, SL, or Scientific and Professional (ST) Mission Area Assistant CIO recruitment actions for consultation regarding position structure and recruitment strategies;

extract_result.purpose: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) policy governing the oversight and management of the Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act (FITARA), Public Law (P.L.) 113-291. FITARA requires that the USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) coordinate FITARA-related activities with other senior Department officials including the following: Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Chief Acquisition Officer (CAO), Chief Operating Officer (COO) (represented by the USDA Deputy Secretary), Senior Procurement Executive (SPE), Chief Human Capital Officer (CHCO), and the Director, Office of Budget and Program Analysis (OBPA). The USDA CIO, CFO, COO, CAO, SPE, CHCO, and OBPA, as a group, will be identified in this DR as the Chief Executive Officers (CXO). The CXOs are tasked with fully defining and understanding the costs of the Department’s information technology (IT) investments, products, and services to be included and incorporated into the USDA budget formulation, budget execution, acquisition, governance, program management, information security, cybersecurity, and IT workforce planning processes.

In response to FITARA and objectives further delineated in M-15-14, USDA developed the  *United States Department of Agriculture Federal Information Technology Acquisition Reform Act Common Baseline and Implementation Plan*  (*USDA Common Baseline Plan*), dated November 14, 2015, which further delineates the role of the USDA CIO in establishing an inclusive, integrated governance process that manages IT as a strategic resource.

This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, employees, appointees, contractors, and others who work for, or on behalf of, USDA and are tasked with the accomplishment and implementation of the requirements identified in FITARA, OMB, and USDA guidance.
